title: spec/lang/_generic/casing.json: what a capital means in a language
description: One shared table (slice 50 section 5; slices 16 and 17). default applies to every base; an entry keyed by a full tag or a primary language overrides it key by key. A language needs an entry only when the default visibly fails for it.

nouns_capitalized.description: Nouns are written with a capital (German), so a capital mid-sentence isn't evidence of a name.

title_case_headlines.description: Headlines capitalise most words (English), so a capital in a Title Case run is weak evidence.

capitalized_pronouns.description: One-letter pronouns always written as a capital (English I).

honorifics.description: Titles before a name, without a final period: a word next to one is part of a name (Mr Will, Sr. Rosa, Herr Wolf).

single_letter_words.description: Ordinary one-letter words of the language (English a; Spanish y, o, a).
